chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), and from Ibn Udhaynah, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:
The Jamarat used to be pelted altogether. I said, 'So can I pelt them (all)?' So he said, 'No. Are you not pleased that you should be doing just as I do?'
ai.seo_question: How should the Jamarat be pelted during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the jurisprudential nuance between pelting all three Jamarat simultaneously versus following the Imam's individual pelting, emphasizing the Shia principle of adhering to the Imam's specific ritual actions. It underscores the importance of imitating the Imam's method to ensure ritual validity and spiritual alignment, a key concept in Shia fiqh derived from the Imams' authority.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Irahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), and from Ibn Azina, from Ibn Bukeyr. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The
Jamarah used to be pelted altogether’. I said, ‘So can I pelt them (all)?’ So heasws said: ‘No. Are you not pleased that you should be doing just as Iasws do?’
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah and from ‘ibn ‘Udhaynah from ibn Bukayr who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘Pebbles were thrown on all of them.’ I then asked, ‘Can I throw on all of them?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, do you not like to do as I do?”’
